note: each line's text sent as a user message through decide (tier 1, no existing memories); a line is marked when the question is at the threshold and its kind is one of constraint, preference, decision, architecture

rows.text: The app is Flask 3 with Jinja templates; each resource has a blueprint in `sundial/routes/` and its templates in `sundial/templates/<resource>/`
Data lives in SQLite through `q()` in `sundial/db.py`; no ORM
SQL goes through `q()` with `?` placeholders and a params tuple; a value is never formatted into the SQL text
Every string shown to people, in a template or a `flash()`, goes through `t()` from `sundial/i18n.py`, with the English text in `sundial/locales/en.json`; no English copy in templates or views
Only `sundial/locales/en.json` is edited by hand; `de.json` and `fr.json` come from the translation vendor's sync, and edits there are overwritten
Dates and times shown to people go through `fmt_date()` and `fmt_time()` from `sundial/dates.py` (the studio's local time); `strftime` is never called in a template or a view
Tunable values (limits, windows, batch sizes) come from `settings.get('name')` with their default in `config/defaults.toml`; no such literal in Python
Every route change comes with a pytest test in `tests/` that goes through the `client` fixture
A migration file that has run anywhere is never edited; every schema change is a new numbered file in `migrations/`
Nothing is committed straight to `main`; work goes on a branch and through a pull request
Log lines may carry booking ids but never a member's name or email address
Commit subjects are one short imperative sentence

Tried Celery with Redis for the confirmation and reminder emails, but the ops box has no Redis and the worker died on every deploy; emails are queued in the `outbox` table with `mail.enqueue()` and sent by `flask send-outbox` from cron
List pages show 25 rows per page (`page_size` in `config/defaults.toml`), with `?page=` starting at 1
Bookings made after 11 pm landed on the next day because times were compared in UTC; bookings are stored and compared in the studio's local time
Prices are integer cents (`price_cents`); never floats
Tried FullCalendar for the week view, but the bundle tripled and it fought the server-rendered pages; the week view is a plain Jinja table
A room's capacity is a column on `rooms`; a booking that would exceed it is refused with a 409
A waiting list for full classes is planned after the autumn term
Staff log in with the session cookie set by `/login`; there is no API token
Double-clicking Book created two bookings; the create route ignores an identical booking made in the last few seconds (`duplicate_window_seconds`)
The bookings export is CSV, read from the database `export_batch_rows` at a time
Reminders go out by email the evening before, through the outbox; SMS stopped when the provider's prices doubled
Moving the queries to SQLAlchemy was abandoned after two days: the generated SQL missed the `(room_id, starts_at)` index and the list page took 4 s; the hand-written SQL through `q()` stays
A booking can be cancelled up to `cancel_window_minutes` before it starts; a later cancellation is kept and marked late
Room names are unique and never renamed; a renamed room gets a new row
An iCal feed per member is planned once members can log in
Form errors are shown with `flash(t('key'), 'error')` above the form, never as inline text next to a field
The studio's timezone is `Europe/Berlin`, set once as `studio_tz` in `config/defaults.toml`
Capacity checks counted cancelled bookings; the count excludes rows with `cancelled_at` set
Tried one-time codes by email for staff login, but the codes arrived minutes late through the outbox cron and staff were locked out; the password login stays
Deploys are a `git pull` and `systemctl restart sundial` on the one host, by hand
Static files are served by Flask from `sundial/static/`; there is no bundler
Outgoing email is a row in the `outbox` table (`mail.enqueue()`); `flask send-outbox` sends what is queued
The API is Fastify 5 in TypeScript (`src/server.ts` builds the app); each resource has a route file in `src/routes/`
Readings and alerts are stored in SQLite through `better-sqlite3` with hand-written SQL in `src/db.ts`; no ORM
Every HTTP route is also declared in `api/openapi.yaml` (path, parameters, responses); `test/contract.test.ts` fails on a route the file does not list
API errors are thrown as `new ApiError(code)` from `src/errors.ts`, with the code added to `ERROR_CODES` there; a route never builds its own `{ message }` with `reply.code(4xx)`
Public ids are 20-character strings from `newId()` in `src/lib/ids.ts`; `crypto.randomUUID()` and the uuid package are not used
Water heights are integer millimetres everywhere: `height_mm` in SQL, fields ending in `Mm` in JSON; never metres or floats
Settings are read from `process.env` in `src/config.ts` only; the rest of `src/` reads `config`
Every route has a test in `test/routes/` that calls it with `app.inject`
Failures are logged with `log` from `src/lib/log.ts` with structured fields, as in `log.warn({ stationId, err }, "noaa fetch failed")`; `console.*` is never used in `src/`
`main` is protected; changes go through a pull request with one review
Outbound HTTP goes through `httpGet` in `src/lib/http.ts` (5 s timeout, one retry); `fetch` is never called directly
Commit subjects are short imperative sentences without ticket numbers
List endpoints take `limit` and `offset`; `limit` defaults to 100 and is capped at 500
Tried WebSockets for live readings, but the proxy closed idle sockets after 60 s and every dashboard reconnected at once; dashboards poll `GET /v1/stations/:id/readings?since=` every 30 s
Tried caching NOAA answers in a module-level `Map`, but memory grew with every station and the process was OOM-killed; upstream answers are cached with `cached()` in `src/lib/cache.ts` (Redis)
`cached(key, ttlSeconds, fn)` in `src/lib/cache.ts` keeps upstream answers in Redis
Readings come from NOAA CO-OPS (`src/upstream/noaa.ts`), polled by `src/poller.ts` inside the API process
Alerts fired on every reading because NOAA's metres were compared with thresholds in millimetres; `noaa.ts` converts at the boundary
Readings around the autumn clock change were stored twice because `at` was local time; `at` is an ISO 8601 UTC string
Timestamps in SQL and JSON are ISO 8601 strings in UTC
An alert fires once when a reading crosses its threshold and arms again only after the height falls below it
Alert emails go out through Postmark from `src/notify.ts`
Prisma was tried for the readings table, but its generated client added 180 MB to the image and cold start doubled; `better-sqlite3` with hand-written SQL stays
Readings older than 90 days (`readingsRetentionDays`) are deleted by the nightly job; nothing reads them after that
Move from SQLite to Postgres once there are more than 50 stations
SMS alerts wait until the Postmark contract covers them
Station ids are NOAA's 7-digit station numbers, kept as strings, never numbers
`GET /v1/stations` ignored a `limit` above the cap silently; it answers 400 `limit_too_large`
Deploys are a Docker image built by GitHub Actions on `main` and pulled by the one VM
The poller runs every minute; NOAA publishes a reading every 6 minutes, so a run with nothing new is normal
Running the poller as a cron job was dropped: overlapping runs double-inserted readings; it is a loop inside the API process
Heights are rounded half up to the millimetre at the NOAA boundary and never rounded again
CORS allows the dashboard origin only (`config.dashboardOrigin`); never `*`
Tests run against a fresh SQLite file per test (`makeTestApp()` in `test/helpers.ts`); the database is never mocked
